identity: The Moonfall Observatory charts the stars over a wood that someone is quietly emptying with marked snares.

quests.title: The Stars Have No Need to Howl
quests.text: I have watched the heavens for years without hearing a star demand an answer; the Briarpack Wolves beneath my window are less considerate. Kill five in the {name:eaves} {zone_area:eaves}, where they roam by day and are more plentiful after dark. A wounded wolf calls its pack, so leave yourself room to retreat.

quests.title: The Wrong Kind of Binding
quests.text: Someone has strung snares between my sighting posts, all stamped with a warden's mark that no honest warden granted. Defeat four Unlicensed Poachers at night in the {name:eaves} {zone_area:eaves}. I use those posts to study where things belong; I can state with some certainty that poachers do not.

quests.title: A Bear in the Calculation
quests.text: My apprentices can account for the motion of the heavens, but their field notes become rather brief whenever a bear arrives. Kill five Bramble Bears by day in the {name:deepwood} {zone_area:deepwood}, so we can resume our measurements. We have already established that the bears object; no further evidence is needed on that point.

quests.title: One Light, Properly Accounted For
quests.text: The Wandering Wisps in the {name:wisp_fen} {zone_area:wisp_fen} keep intruding on my observations. Hunt them after dark, the only time they appear, and bring me one Bound Wisp Mote for calibrating the great lens. It will be satisfying to put a little of that troublesome light to work.

quests.title: A Clear View Needs Sound Wood
quests.text: The poachers have pulled down my sighting posts; without them, a hundred nights of careful work become a collection of guesses. Bring me ten planks of any wood here at the Observatory so I can rebuild them. Craft the planks wherever convenient, and let us have something steady beneath the moving sky again.

quests.title: A Warden in Name Alone
quests.text: Follow enough false marks and you find the hand that makes them: {name:snarewarden_bracken}. Vetch and Rusk answered to him, and he waits {dir_from_giver:snarewarden_bracken}, by day and night. Find and defeat him. A warden should leave the wood alive behind him, not measured out in snares.

quests.title: Optional: An Astronomer's Ankles
quests.text: A steady stance is essential to observation, and the Barnacle Pinchers on the {name:moonstrand} {dir_from_giver:moonstrand} make it impossible to maintain one. Kill five by day, before I set up for my night's work. Spare the Bank Crabs; they have never tried to dismantle the observer.

quests.title: Optional: Teeth Along the Trail
quests.text: The marks continue through the {name:elderwood} {zone_area:elderwood}, where Bramble Bears make daylight travel a costly undertaking. Kill six by day to ease the search for whoever lays those snares. I doubt the bears care whose business they protect; that does little to comfort the searchers.

quests.title: Optional: Thread Across the Stars
quests.text: Briar-Web Spiders stretch their webs through the {name:elderwood} {zone_area:elderwood} at night, giving the snare-setters convenient markers and everyone else a faceful of silk. Kill six after dark. I prefer to admire fine weaving when it is not attached to my eyebrows.

quests.title: Bounty: Keep the View Clear
quests.text: Each clear night should add a little to our knowledge, not another layer of web to our faces. Kill six Briar-Web Spiders after dark in the {name:deepwood} {zone_area:deepwood} and return for the Observatory's payment. The bounty is repeatable; the spiders appear no more inclined to finish their work than I am.
